habitat: Grasslands, agricultural land and human settlements
range: Widely introduced worldwide. The atlas represents a laboratory specimen.
summary: Explore how a house mouse uses its whiskers to sample nearby surfaces. Compare its intact exterior with a laboratory anatomy atlas, then investigate colour detection and ultrasonic calls.

visual.description: Scientific atlas in instructional colors. CT and cryosection source surfaces share a reference frame with traced and simulated additions.

behaviors.label: Reference stance
behaviors.description: The scanned specimen was repositioned into an estimated standing posture.

behaviors.label: Tail flexion
behaviors.description: Six-second lateral bend and return. Bone regions, veins and outer tail share the same deformation. Timing and angles are authored.
behaviors.studyNote: Display time in seconds. The recorded animal and the anatomical atlas are different specimens.

behaviors.label: Whisker sweep
behaviors.description: Three slowed bilateral sweeps around the whisker roots. Sofroniew et al. tracked the C2 whisker during treadmill running. The display extends that pattern to the array at 0.5 cycles per second.
behaviors.studyNote: Display time in seconds. The recorded animal and the anatomical atlas are different specimens.

behaviors.label: Whiskers during steering
behaviors.description: One whisker array shifts forward as the other shifts back, as observed during treadmill steering. The body stays in a reference stance. The shift angle and six-second sequence are illustrative.
behaviors.studyNote: Display time in seconds. The recorded animal and the anatomical atlas are different specimens.
